---
title: "How xdssat differs from common DSSAT use"
subtitle: "From one field and one weather station to every rice cell of an island, with the engine unchanged"
---

```{ojs}
import {withDownload, adminMarks, cellFeatures, fmt} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
summary = FileAttachment("../java/data/summary.json").json()
runs = FileAttachment("../java/data/runs.json").json()
cells = FileAttachment("../java/data/grid_cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
outline = FileAttachment("../java/data/java_outline.geojson").json()
provinces = FileAttachment("../java/data/provinces.geojson").json()
districtsGeo = FileAttachment("../java/data/districts.geojson").json()
grid = FileAttachment("../java/data/grid_yearly.json").json()
schema = FileAttachment("../java/data/nc_schema.csv").csv()
ncAttrs = FileAttachment("../java/data/nc_attrs.json").json()
cur = summary.current
mapW = Math.min(width, 960)
```

## Side by side

| | Common DSSAT use | xdssat |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of simulation | A field experiment: one plot, a few treatments | One stratum = one 0.1° weather cell x one water regime, one treatment per season |
| Weather | One station file, often typed in or converted by hand | One `.WTH` per weather cell, written from a gridded weather input such as AgERA5 (`src/wth.py`) |
| Soil | A profile picked from a DSSAT soil file (WISE, local survey) | One profile per weather cell, from SoilGrids 2.0 or from your own profiles (`src/soils.py`, `src/soilprep.py`) |
| Management | The experiment's own FileX, edited in the DSSAT shell or XBuild | A template FileX; every unit copies one treatment and shifts all its dates (`src/filex.py`) |
| Planting date | Fixed by the experiment | Per cell from rainfall onset, per zone, or uniform (`src/management.py`) |
| Running | The DSSAT shell, one batch, one process | Chunks of up to `--chunk-size` units, each its own folder and `dscsm048` process, `--workers` in parallel (`src/runner.py`) |
| Failures | The batch stops at the first fatal input error | The failing unit is named from `ERROR.OUT`, dropped, the rest rerun; listed in `failed.csv` |
| Output | `.OUT` text files and `summary.csv` per run | `summary.csv` joined to the strata, then a CF-1.10 netCDF on the weather grid (`src/outputs.py`) |
| Area | Results per hectare of the plot | Every result carries the rice ha it stands for, so regional totals are sums |

The engine itself is not touched: xdssat builds or reuses the stock DSSAT-CSM 4.8 executable
[@jones2003; @dssatcsmos] and talks to it only through its own text files.

## Gridding: crop pixels to weather cells to strata

Each pixel of the crop mask goes to the weather cell that holds its centre, carrying its hectares; the water
regime, region and zone maps are read at the same pixel (any grid and CRS, see [Input data](data.qmd)). Within
a cell all of the crop shares one weather series and one soil profile, so the only split that changes the
simulation is the water regime: a cell has an irrigated stratum, a rain-fed stratum, or both.

In the Java case study the rice fields, irrigation class, province, district and zone are burned onto one
100 m equal-area grid (ESRI:54034), where one pixel is one hectare, and the weather cells are AgERA5's 0.1°.

```{ojs}
strataCount = d3.rollups(cells, v => v.length, d => (d.ha_irrigated > 0 ? "irrigated" : "") + (d.ha_irrigated > 0 && d.ha_rainfed > 0 ? " + " : "") + (d.ha_rainfed > 0 ? "rain-fed" : ""))
  .map(([k, n]) => ({strata: k, cells: n}))
strataText = strataCount.map(d => `${fmt.int(d.cells)} cells with ${d.strata}`).join(", ")
```

For the current run: ${fmt.int(cur.cells)} cells and ${fmt.int(cur.strata)} strata
: ${strataText}.

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 760), height: 300, marginLeft: 55,
  x: {type: "log", label: "Rice area in the cell, ha (log scale)", grid: true},
  y: {label: "Cells", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectY(cells.map(d => ({ha: d.ha, kind: d.ha_irrigated > 0 && d.ha_rainfed > 0 ? "both regimes" : d.ha_irrigated > 0 ? "irrigated only" : "rain-fed only"})),
      Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {x: "ha", fill: "kind", thresholds: d3.ticks(0, 4.2, 30).map(v => 10 ** v), tip: true})),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "xdssat-cells-rice-ha-histogram")
```

The rice area per cell spans several orders of magnitude, so weighting matters: a cell with a few hectares of
rice should not count as much as one with ten thousand. Every stratum carries its hectares into the outputs.

## Data preparation: netCDF and GeoTIFF to WTH, SOL and FileX

The Java case study's preparation, from its source files to the engine's input files. Other sources go through
the prepare scripts described in [Input data](data.qmd) and end in the same standard inputs.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"theme": "neutral"}}%%
flowchart TB
  A1["AgERA5 netCDF<br/>global, per variable-year"] -->|build_agera5_cache.py| B1["agera5/idn/VAR/<br/>int16, DSSAT units"]
  A2["SoilGrids VRT + tiles<br/>250 m"] -->|build_soilgrids_cache.py| B2["soilgrids/idn/*.tif"]
  A3["Rice, irrigation, zones,<br/>districts: polygons"] -->|prepare_rasters.py| B3["rasters/idn_*.tif<br/>100 m, 1 px = 1 ha"]
  B2 -->|prepare_soils.py| B4["soils/java.SOL<br/>1 profile per cell"]
  B3 --> B4
  B3 -->|run_aoi.py| C1["strata.csv<br/>cell x water regime, ha"]
  C1 --> C2["units.csv<br/>one row per season"]
  B1 --> C3
  B4 --> C3
  C2 --> C3["chunk folders:<br/>FileX + WTH + SOIL.SOL"]
  C3 --> C4["dscsm048 x workers"]
  C4 --> C5["summary.csv + failed.csv"]
  C5 -->|outputs.py| C6["run .nc, CF-1.10"]
```

- **Weather**: per cell, a seven-digit-date `.WTH` file covering all years, so one file serves every season
  (`src/wth.py`; `TAV` and `AMP` computed from the series).
- **Soil**: `SOIL.SOL` in each chunk folder holds exactly the profiles that chunk uses; the engine looks there
  first (`src/sol.py`).
- **FileX**: one experiment per chunk, one treatment per cell-season. Field, weather station, soil ID and every
  date of the template treatment change; identical levels are written once (`src/filex.py`).

## Chunked parallel runs

A chunk is one folder, one FileX with up to `--chunk-size` treatments, one `dscsm048` process. DSSAT clears its
fixed-name output files at start-up, so each process needs its own folder; and a fatal input error stops the
whole FileX, so the runner finds the culprit in `ERROR.OUT`, removes it and reruns the rest. The table lists
every run folder in the cache.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(runs, {
  columns: ["run", "status", "mode", "cultivar", "n", "slpf", "slpf_rainfed", "slpf_table", "tcldf", "seasons", "failed", "minutes", "workers", "chunk_size", "nc_mb"],
  header: {run: "Run", status: "Status", mode: "Mode", cultivar: "Cultivar", n: "N kg/ha", slpf: "SLPF", slpf_rainfed: "SLPF rain-fed", slpf_table: "SLPF table", tcldf: "TCLDF", seasons: "Seasons", failed: "Failed", minutes: "Minutes", workers: "Workers", chunk_size: "Chunk", nc_mb: "netCDF MB"},
  format: {seasons: fmt.int}, layout: "auto", rows: 10})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 760), height: 40 + runs.length * 28, marginLeft: 260,
  x: {label: "Wall time, minutes", grid: true},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(runs, {y: "run", x: "minutes", fill: d => d.current ? "#2a7f62" : "#9bb8ad", tip: true, channels: {seasons: "seasons", failed: "failed"}, sort: {y: "x"}})
  ]
}), "xdssat-run-times")
```

::: {.source-note}
From each run's `run_info.json`. Status labels: "current" is the run the site is exported from; "stale" marks
runs made before a correction of the initial soil nitrogen, kept for comparison (`export_data.py`).
:::

## CF-compliant netCDF output

Each run ends with one netCDF file on the weather grid, dimensions `(system, time, lat, lon)`. A *system* is a
season and water regime that was simulated (`wet_irrigated`, `wet_rainfed`, `dry_irrigated`), so no slab is
empty by construction: rain-fed rice has no dry season. `time` is 1 August of each agricultural year; the
actual dates are variables. Area variables make regional totals a plain sum: the mean yield of any region is
`production.sum() / harvested_area.sum() * 1000` kg/ha.

```{ojs}
viewof ncSys = Inputs.radio(new Map(Object.keys(grid.systems).map(k => [k.replace("_", ", "), k])), {value: Object.keys(grid.systems)[0], label: "system"})
viewof ncYear = Inputs.range([d3.min(grid.years), d3.max(grid.years)], {step: 1, value: d3.max(grid.years), label: "time (season year)"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const t = grid.years.indexOf(ncYear);
  const vals = grid.systems[ncSys][t];
  const rows = grid.lat.map((lat, i) => ({lat, lon: grid.lon[i], v: vals[i]})).filter(d => d.v != null);
  const meanY = d3.mean(rows, d => d.v);
  return withDownload(Plot.plot({
    width: mapW, height: Math.round(mapW * 0.42),
    projection: {type: "mercator", domain: outline},
    caption: `yield[system=${ncSys}, time=${ncYear}-08-01], ${grid.run}; ${rows.length} cells, unweighted cell mean ${fmt.int(meanY)} kg/ha`,
    color: {type: "linear", scheme: "YlGn", domain: [2000, 7000], clamp: true, legend: true, label: "yield (HWAH), kg/ha dry matter"},
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(provinces, {fill: "#f1f1f1", clip: true}),
      Plot.geo(cellFeatures(rows).features, Plot.centroid({fill: d => d.properties.v, title: d => `${fmt.int(d.properties.v)} kg/ha`, tip: true})),
      ...adminMarks(Plot, provinces, districtsGeo)
    ]
  }), `xdssat-nc-yield-${ncSys}-${ncYear}`);
}
```

The variables in the file (read from the current run's netCDF by `export_data.py`):

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(schema, {columns: ["name", "kind", "dims", "dtype", "units", "long_name", "standard_name"], rows: 30, layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(Object.entries(ncAttrs).map(([k, v]) => ({attribute: k, value: v})), {rows: 20, layout: "auto", width: {value: 600}})
```
